Su-35.name: Su-35S Flanker-E
Su-35.description: Russia's most capable in-service fighter. Super-maneuverable with thrust vectoring and Irbis-E PESA radar. The backbone of modern Russian air superiority forces, extensively deployed in Syria and Ukraine.

Su-35S.name: Su-35S Flanker-E
Su-35S.description: Russia's most capable in-service fighter. Super-maneuverable with thrust vectoring and Irbis-E PESA radar.

Su-30SM.name: Su-30SM Flanker-H
Su-30SM.description: Two-seat multirole variant of the Flanker family. India's main air superiority fighter (as Su-30MKI). Russia operates ~130 for both air-to-air and strike missions.

Su-27.name: Su-27 Flanker
Su-27.description: The original Flanker — designed to counter the F-15. Exceptional maneuverability and range. Being replaced by Su-35S but still widely used.

Su-27SM.name: Su-27SM Flanker
Su-27SM.description: Modernized Su-27 with upgraded avionics, glass cockpit, and precision strike capability. Can carry guided weapons unlike the original.

Su-33.name: Su-33 Flanker-D
Su-33.description: Navalized Flanker for Admiral Kuznetsov carrier. Folding wings, reinforced landing gear, canards. Only ~20 in service.

Su-34.name: Su-34 Fullback
Su-34.description: Modern strike fighter replacing the Su-24. Distinctive flat nose with side-by-side cockpit. Russia's primary precision strike platform in Ukraine. ~150 in service.

Su-24.name: Su-24M Fencer
Su-24.description: Variable-sweep wing strike aircraft. Primary Russian tactical bomber, used extensively in Syria and Ukraine. Being replaced by Su-34.

Su-24M.name: Su-24M Fencer
Su-24M.description: Variable-sweep wing strike aircraft. Being replaced by Su-34 but still widely deployed.

Su-24MK.name: Su-24MK Fencer (Export)
Su-24MK.description: Export variant operated by Iran. Iran's most capable strike aircraft, acquired from the Soviet Union.

Su-25.name: Su-25 Grach
Su-25.description: Russia's equivalent to the A-10. Heavily armored with titanium cockpit bathtub. Heavy losses in Ukraine due to MANPADS.

Su-25SM.name: Su-25SM Grach
Su-25SM.description: Modernized Frogfoot with glass cockpit, GPS, and precision munitions capability.

Su-57.name: Su-57 Felon
Su-57.description: Russia's 5th gen stealth fighter. Only ~10 delivered. Internal weapons bays, supercruise. Limited use in Ukraine for standoff strikes.

MiG-29.name: MiG-29 Fulcrum
MiG-29.description: Lightweight air superiority fighter designed to counter the F-16. Exceptional close-combat maneuverability with helmet-mounted sight.

MiG-29A.name: MiG-29A Fulcrum
MiG-29A.description: Early export variant operated by Iran. Limited numbers (~25) but Iran's most modern fighter.

MiG-29K.name: MiG-29K Fulcrum-D
MiG-29K.description: Navalized MiG-29 for carrier operations. Folding wings, arresting hook. Replacing Su-33 on Admiral Kuznetsov.

MiG-29SMT.name: MiG-29SMT Fulcrum-E
MiG-29SMT.description: Deep modernization with enlarged fuel tank spine, Zhuk-ME radar, and precision strike capability.

MiG-31BM.name: MiG-31BM Foxhound
MiG-31BM.description: World's fastest combat aircraft in service. MiG-31K variant carries the Kinzhal hypersonic missile. Four aircraft can control 800km of airspace.

Tu-95.name: Tu-95MS Bear
Tu-95.description: Iconic strategic bomber with contra-rotating turboprops. Loudest aircraft ever built. Regularly launches Kh-101 strikes against Ukraine from Caspian standoff range. ~60 in service.

Tu-95MS.name: Tu-95MS Bear
Tu-95MS.description: Modernized Bear. Primary Russian cruise missile carrier. Regular strikes on Ukraine from standoff positions.

Tu-160.name: Tu-160 White Swan
Tu-160.description: Largest and heaviest combat aircraft ever built. Variable-sweep supersonic strategic bomber. Only ~17 in service at Engels-2. Used to launch cruise missiles at Ukraine.

Tu-22M.name: Tu-22M3 Backfire
Tu-22M.description: Variable-sweep supersonic bomber for maritime strike. Used for carpet bombing in Syria and Ukraine with unguided FABs. ~60 in service.

Tu-22M3.name: Tu-22M3 Backfire
Tu-22M3.description: Variable-sweep supersonic bomber. Carpet bombing with unguided FABs in Ukraine. ~60 in service.

Il-76.name: Il-76 Candid
Il-76.description: Soviet heavy transport workhorse. Can carry tanks, troops, and heavy equipment. High activity indicates troop/equipment movements.

Il-78.name: Il-78 Midas
Il-78.description: Il-76 based tanker. Extends range of Russian combat aircraft. Critical enabler for long-range bomber operations.

A-50.name: A-50 Mainstay
A-50.description: Russia's primary AWACS platform based on Il-76. Shmel radar dome. Only ~10 in service. Loss of even one is strategically significant.

An-26.name: An-26 Curl
An-26.description: Light tactical transport for cargo and paratroopers. Workhorse of Soviet-era transport aviation.

An-124.name: An-124 Ruslan
An-124.description: One of world's largest aircraft. Can carry tanks and S-400 systems. ~10 in Russian military service.

Il-20.name: Il-20 Coot-A
Il-20.description: Electronic intelligence aircraft based on Il-18 airliner. Used for signals intelligence gathering along NATO borders.

Ka-52.name: Ka-52 Alligator
Ka-52.description: Russia's most advanced attack helicopter with coaxial rotors. Side-by-side cockpit with ejection seats. Extensive combat use in Ukraine.

Mi-8.name: Mi-8/17 Hip
Mi-8.description: Most produced helicopter ever (17,000+). Backbone of Russian rotary-wing ops.

F-15.name: F-15 Eagle / Strike Eagle
F-15.description: Undefeated in air combat (104-0). F-15E Strike Eagle variant is a dual-role fighter-bomber. 48th FW at RAF Lakenheath.

F-16.name: F-16 Fighting Falcon
F-16.description: Most produced Western fighter (4,600+). Lightweight, affordable, highly maneuverable. Being supplied to Ukraine as F-16AM/BM.

F-22.name: F-22 Raptor
F-22.description: World's first operational 5th gen fighter. Stealth, supercruise, supermaneuverability. Only 187 built. Never exported.

FA-18.name: F/A-18E/F Super Hornet
FA-18.description: US Navy's primary carrier-based fighter. Replaced F-14 Tomcat. E model is single-seat, F model is two-seat.

B-52.name: B-52H Stratofortress
B-52.description: In service since 1955, expected to fly until 2050s. 76 in active service. Can carry 70,000 lbs of ordnance.

B-1B.name: B-1B Lancer
B-1B.description: Variable-sweep supersonic bomber. Largest internal payload of any US bomber. Used extensively in Afghanistan and Iraq.

C-130.name: C-130 Hercules / Super Hercules
C-130.description: Most versatile military transport ever built. 2,500+ produced. Can land on dirt strips. Variants: tanker, gunship, ISR, weather.

C-17.name: C-17 Globemaster III
C-17.description: Can carry M1 Abrams tanks. Capable of short-field tactical landings. 275 built. The backbone of US strategic airlift.

C-5.name: C-5M Super Galaxy
C-5.description: One of the largest military aircraft in the world. Can carry 2 M1 Abrams tanks or 6 Apache helicopters.

KC-135.name: KC-135 Stratotanker
KC-135.description: USAF's primary tanker since 1957. Can refuel any NATO aircraft. 396 still in service. Being replaced by KC-46.

KC-10.name: KC-10 Extender
KC-10.description: DC-10 based tanker/cargo aircraft. Larger than KC-135. Can refuel and carry cargo simultaneously. Being retired.

E-3.name: E-3 Sentry AWACS
E-3.description: Flying command center with 30ft rotodome radar. Can track 600 targets at 400km range. The backbone of NATO air defense.

E-8.name: E-8 Joint STARS
E-8.description: Ground surveillance radar aircraft. Tracks moving vehicles and troops. Used in every US conflict since Desert Storm.

P-3C.name: P-3C Orion
P-3C.description: Maritime patrol and anti-submarine warfare aircraft. Being replaced by P-8A Poseidon.

F-14A Tomcat.name: F-14A Tomcat
F-14A Tomcat.description: Iran is the only country still operating the F-14. ~40 airworthy. Used for long-range fleet defense with Phoenix missiles. Iconic variable-sweep fighter from Top Gun.

F-4E Phantom.name: F-4E Phantom II
F-4E Phantom.description: Vietnam-era fighter still operated by Iran. ~60 in service. Battle-proven in Iran-Iraq War. Iran's workhorse strike fighter.

F-5E Tiger II.name: F-5E Tiger II
F-5E Tiger II.description: Lightweight export fighter. Iran operates ~60. Basis for Iran's domestic Saeqeh and Kowsar fighters.

Saeqeh.name: HESA Saeqeh
Saeqeh.description: Iranian domestic fighter based on F-5 with twin vertical stabilizers. Propaganda claims of 'advanced' capability disputed by Western analysts.

Kowsar.name: HESA Kowsar
Kowsar.description: Iran's 'indigenous' fighter — essentially an F-5 with a new avionics suite and HUD. Limited production.

fighter.name: Unidentified Fighter
fighter.description: Fighter-class aircraft detected. Specific type not classified.

aircraft.name: Unidentified Aircraft
aircraft.description: Aircraft detected but type not classified.

J-20.name: Chengdu J-20 Mighty Dragon
J-20.description: China's 5th-gen stealth fighter. Internal weapons bays, AESA radar, canard-delta configuration. ~200 in service. China's answer to F-22.

J-16.name: Shenyang J-16
J-16.description: Chinese Flanker derivative for strike missions. AESA radar, advanced EW suite. ~300 in service.

H-6K.name: Xian H-6K
H-6K.description: Modernized Tu-16 derivative. China's primary nuclear delivery platform and cruise missile carrier. Patrols South China Sea.

Y-20.name: Xian Y-20 Kunpeng
Y-20.description: China's indigenous strategic airlifter. Can carry ZTQ-15 tanks, ballistic missiles. Tanker variant (YY-20) also in service.

Y-9.name: Shaanxi Y-9
Y-9.description: Chinese C-130 equivalent. Variants include ELINT (Y-9JB), maritime patrol (Y-9Q), and AEW (KJ-500 platform).

KJ-500.name: KJ-500 AEW&C
KJ-500.description: China's latest AWACS based on Y-9. Triple AESA array in dorsal rotodome. Can track fighters at 450km range.

Typhoon.name: Eurofighter Typhoon
Typhoon.description: Europe's primary air superiority fighter. Canard-delta, supercruise capable. Operated by UK, Germany, Italy, Spain, Austria, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait.

Eurofighter.name: Eurofighter Typhoon
Eurofighter.description: Europe's primary air superiority fighter. Operated by UK, Germany, Italy, Spain.

Rafale.name: Dassault Rafale
Rafale.description: France's omnirole fighter. Carrier and land-based variants. Nuclear strike capable with ASMP-A. Exported to India, Egypt, Qatar, Greece, UAE, Indonesia.

Rafale DM.name: Dassault Rafale DM (Egypt)
Rafale DM.description: Egyptian export variant. 24 delivered. Egypt's most advanced fighter.

Tornado.name: Panavia Tornado
Tornado.description: Variable-sweep strike aircraft. IDS (interdictor) and ECR (SEAD) variants. Operated by Germany, Italy, Saudi Arabia. Being replaced by Typhoon/F-35.

Gripen E.name: Saab Gripen E
Gripen E.description: Latest Gripen variant with AESA radar. Can operate from road bases. Exported to Brazil, South Africa, Czech Republic, Hungary, Thailand.

F-35A.name: F-35A Lightning II
F-35A.description: 5th-gen stealth fighter with sensor fusion. Three variants: A (CTOL), B (STOVL), C (carrier). 1000+ delivered to 17 nations.

F-35I Adir.name: F-35I Adir
F-35I Adir.description: Israeli F-35 with custom EW systems and C4I integration. Israel is the first country to use F-35 in combat.

F-15E.name: F-15E Strike Eagle
F-15E.description: Air-to-ground optimized F-15. Conformal fuel tanks, LANTIRN/Sniper pods. The backbone of USAF precision strike.

F-15I Ra'am.name: F-15I Ra'am (Thunder)
F-15I Ra'am.description: Israeli F-15E variant with indigenous weapons and EW. Can reach Iran without refueling. 25 in service.

F-15K.name: F-15K Slam Eagle
F-15K.description: South Korean F-15E variant. 61 in service. Primary deep-strike platform against North Korea.

F-15SA.name: F-15SA Strike Eagle
F-15SA.description: Most advanced F-15 variant. Fly-by-wire, AESA radar, digital EW. 84 delivered to Saudi Arabia.

F-16C.name: F-16C Fighting Falcon
F-16C.description: Block 50/52 variant with improved radar and engines.

F-16AM.name: F-16AM Fighting Falcon (MLU)
F-16AM.description: Mid-Life Update F-16A/B with modern avionics. Operated by Belgium, Netherlands, Norway, Denmark, Portugal, Jordan.

F-16V.name: F-16V Viper
F-16V.description: Latest F-16 with AESA radar, modern cockpit. Taiwan's primary fighter (upgraded + new-build).

F-16E Block 60.name: F-16E Block 60 Desert Falcon
F-16E Block 60.description: UAE-exclusive advanced F-16 with conformal fuel tanks and AESA radar. 80 in service.

F-16C Block 52.name: F-16C Block 52+
F-16C Block 52.description: Pakistan operates 18 F-16C/D Block 52+ with advanced targeting pods.

F-2A.name: Mitsubishi F-2
F-2A.description: Japanese F-16 derivative with larger wing and domestic weapons. Primary anti-ship strike role. 62 in service.

CF-18.name: CF-188 Hornet
CF-18.description: Canadian F/A-18A/B. 76 in service. Being replaced by F-35A. NORAD QRA duties.

EF-18.name: EF-18 Hornet (Spain)
EF-18.description: Spanish F/A-18 Hornet. Being replaced by Eurofighter Typhoon.

F/A-18F.name: F/A-18F Super Hornet
F/A-18F.description: Two-seat Super Hornet. Australia operates 24 alongside F-35A.

KF-21.name: KAI KF-21 Boramae
KF-21.description: South Korea's indigenous 4.5-gen fighter. Semi-stealth design. First flight 2022. 120 planned.

JF-17.name: CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder
JF-17.description: Sino-Pakistani lightweight fighter. Pakistan's most numerous fighter (~150). Block 3 has AESA radar.

F-7.name: Chengdu F-7 Airguard
F-7.description: Chinese MiG-21 derivative. Operated by Iran, Bangladesh, Myanmar. Very limited capability.

Mirage 2000-5.name: Dassault Mirage 2000-5
Mirage 2000-5.description: Advanced Mirage 2000 with RDY radar. Operated by France, Taiwan, Qatar, UAE.

Mirage 2000-9.name: Dassault Mirage 2000-9
Mirage 2000-9.description: UAE's upgraded Mirage 2000 with advanced weapons. 68 in service.

MiG-29M2.name: MiG-29M2 Fulcrum-E
MiG-29M2.description: Russia's latest MiG-29 export variant. Egypt operates 46. AESA radar, precision strike capable.

Su-30MKI.name: Su-30MKI Flanker-H
Su-30MKI.description: India's most capable fighter. 272 in service. Can carry BrahMos supersonic cruise missile.

A400M.name: Airbus A400M Atlas
A400M.description: European military airlifter. Turboprop, rough-field capable. Operated by France, Germany, UK, Spain, Turkey, Belgium, Malaysia.

C-130J.name: C-130J Super Hercules
C-130J.description: Latest Hercules. Faster, higher, further than C-130H. 500+ delivered to 22 nations.

C-130E.name: C-130E Hercules
C-130E.description: Early C-130 variant. Still operated by Pakistan, Turkey.

C-2.name: Kawasaki C-2
C-2.description: Japan's indigenous strategic transport. Can carry 120 troops or MIM-104 Patriot. Faster than C-17 but smaller.

E-767.name: Boeing E-767 AWACS
E-767.description: 767-based AWACS. Only Japan operates 4. AN/APY-2 radar. Superior endurance to E-3.

E-737.name: Boeing E-7A Wedgetail (Korea)
E-737.description: 737-based AEW&C. MESA AESA radar. Also operated by Australia, Turkey, UK.

E-7.name: Boeing E-7 Wedgetail
E-7.description: NATO's next-gen AWACS replacing E-3. MESA AESA radar with 360° coverage.

E-7 Wedgetail.name: Boeing E-7 Wedgetail
E-7 Wedgetail.description: RAF's E-3 replacement. 5 ordered for UK.

E-3A.name: E-3A Sentry AWACS (NATO)
E-3A.description: NATO-operated E-3 AWACS fleet based at Geilenkirchen, Germany.

E-3F.name: E-3F Sentry (France)
E-3F.description: French Air Force E-3 variant. 4 in service at Avord.

E-2K.name: E-2K Hawkeye (Taiwan)
E-2K.description: Taiwanese E-2 Hawkeye variant. 6 in service. Critical for Taiwan Strait surveillance.

G550 CAEW.name: IAI EL/W-2085 (G550 CAEW)
G550 CAEW.description: Israeli AWACS on Gulfstream G550 platform. AESA conformal arrays. Also exported to Italy, Singapore.

KC-767.name: KC-767 (Japan)
KC-767.description: 767-based tanker. Japan operates 4. Can refuel fighters via boom or drogue.

KC-330.name: Airbus KC-330 Cygnus (Korea)
KC-330.description: A330 MRTT variant for South Korea. 4 in service. Can refuel any NATO fighter.

KC-130.name: KC-130 Hercules Tanker
KC-130.description: C-130 tanker variant with underwing refueling pods. USMC primary tanker.

A330 MRTT.name: Airbus A330 MRTT
A330 MRTT.description: Wide-body tanker/transport. Operated by UK (Voyager), France, Singapore, UAE, Australia, South Korea.

Voyager.name: Airbus Voyager KC2/KC3
Voyager.description: RAF's A330 MRTT. 14 in service. Can refuel via boom and hose-drogue simultaneously.

Boeing 707.name: Boeing 707 Tanker/Transport
Boeing 707.description: IAF 707 tanker/transport fleet. Used for aerial refueling, VIP, and EW missions.

P-1.name: Kawasaki P-1
P-1.description: Japan's indigenous P-3 replacement. Fly-by-light controls, 4 turbofans. Superior to P-8 in some ASW capabilities.

P-8A.name: Boeing P-8A Poseidon
P-8A.description: 737-based maritime patrol aircraft replacing P-3C. Used by US, UK, Australia, India, Norway.

P-8A Poseidon.name: Boeing P-8A Poseidon
P-8A Poseidon.description: Maritime patrol replacing P-3C. UK operates from RAF Lossiemouth.

ATL2.name: Dassault ATL2 Atlantique 2
ATL2.description: French maritime patrol. 18 in service. Regular Atlantic and Indian Ocean patrols.

RF-4E.name: RF-4E Phantom (Recon)
RF-4E.description: Reconnaissance Phantom with cameras instead of weapons. Iran operates a small fleet for strategic ISR.

A-50EI.name: A-50EI Phalcon (India)
A-50EI.description: Indian A-50 with Israeli EL/W-2090 Phalcon AESA radar. 3 in service.

Shahed-129 UAV.name: Shahed-129
Shahed-129 UAV.description: Iran's primary armed UAV. MQ-1 Predator equivalent. Used in Syria, Iraq, Yemen.

Mohajer UAV.name: Mohajer-6
Mohajer UAV.description: Iranian tactical drone. Exported to Russia for use in Ukraine. Can carry precision-guided munitions.
